text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's civil defence service said it had found the body of an unidentified man in the southern town of Zlatograd who probably drowned in floods in the Rodopi mountain region. Two women drowned in Zlatograd at the weekend.
-- Bulgarian-Russian gas joint venture Topenergy said its business plan foresaw the construction of 650 km of gas pipeline in Bulgaria by 2010.
-- The Bulgarian National Bank is expected to issue a 10,000 lev note on December 10 because of the sharp fall of the lev against the dollar.
-- Bulgaria's cabinet began discussions on two versions of next year's draft budget, one of which plans revenue and expenditure assuming that a currency board will be introduced.
-- Private insurance company Ferostrad, in which Bulgarian State Railways has a 30 percent stake, raised its capital to 200 million levs from 80 million levs, a senior company official said.
-- Bulgaria has exported meat and livestock worth some $94.4 million for the first nine months of 1996, which is 2.9 percent of the country's total commodity exports.

-- Public transport in Sofia and other major cities is expected to be halted on Wednesday for a few hours as drivers will join the strike organised by Bulgaria's biggest union organisation, the Confederation of Independent Trade Unions, union officials said. They are seeking a cabinet reshuffle and early parliamentary elections.

-- Fuel shortages in Bulgaria are the result of technical problems with the Novorosiisk oil pipeline and a delay in the arrival of Bulgarian tankers from Russia, an official of the state fuel supplier Petrol said.
-- Bulgaria has bought 120,000 tonnes of wheat from Argentina at the price of $168.75 per tonne for December delivery.
-- Bulgaria's state Expressbank is expected to raise its capital today to 3.538 billion levs from 713 million levs, an Expressbank senior official said.
